The measures behind every board and chart, as one read. `GET /v1/analytics/measures` describes the whole space so nothing has to be hard-coded; `GET /v1/analytics` answers one measure over one window, optionally split by one dimension; `POST /v1/analytics/query` answers a board's worth in one round trip.

Every payload is self-describing, because a number without its unit is a bug waiting to happen: it states its unit and currency (money is integer MINOR units, never converted here), whether it is a value AT an instant or a sum OVER a window, when it was computed, and — where the history is only partly known — exactly which periods are missing. A cut that cannot be made answers 422 with a sentence naming what can.

## Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | [`/v1/analytics`](/help/developers/api-reference/analytics/one-measure) | One measure, over one window, optionally split by one dimension |
| `GET` | [`/v1/analytics/measures`](/help/developers/api-reference/analytics/every-measure-that-can-be-asked-for) | Every measure that can be asked for, and how it may be cut |
| `POST` | [`/v1/analytics/query`](/help/developers/api-reference/analytics/several-measures-in-one-round-trip) | Several measures in one round trip |
| `GET` | [`/v1/analytics/sync`](/help/developers/api-reference/analytics/when-the-figures-were-last-refreshed) | When the figures were last refreshed |
| `GET` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/reports/usage_margin`](/help/developers/api-reference/analytics/usage-margin) | Usage margin |
